blocks.text: The AI Security Dashboard provides a centralized, at-a-glance view of your organization’s AI application usage and risk posture. From the UI, it brings together key insights, such as which AI apps are being used, usage trends over time, and the most active users or groups, so you can quickly understand where AI is being adopted and where governance may be needed.

The Dashboard is designed to help you move from visibility to action. You can use it to identify sanctioned vs. shadow AI usage, spot unusual spikes in activity, and prioritize AI services that may require tighter controls. The visual widgets and summary cards make it easy to drill into details and pivot to related views (for example, inventory or policy areas) to investigate and respond.
The AI Security Dashboard provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Attain a unified dashboard experience for tracking AI activity, adoption, and risk signals in one place.
Gain a high-level view of your organization’s traffic to public AI services, including overall volume, active users, and the top departments generating AI traffic.
Quickly understand adoption and concentration of use, spot unusual spikes, and prioritize governance and controls where AI activity is highest.
Connects dashboard insights to AI application inventory and AI infrastructure across Gen AI, Embedded AI, and MCP servers, Agents, Apps, etc., helping teams manage AI usage continuously.

blocks.heading: About the AI Security Dashboard Page

blocks.text: On the AI Security Dashboard page, (AI Security > Dashboard), you can view the following widgets and tabs:

blocks.item: Public AI Traffic Overview: View the total traffic volume and user count for Public AI apps discovered across your organization. You can also see the Top 5 Apps or Top 5 Departments in a bar chart. To drill down, click Details to open the Public AI- Overview page.

AI Application by Categories: View the count of newly discovered apps and risky apps. You can also see the distribution of GenAI and Desktop AI apps across your organization in a donut chart. To drill down, click Details to open the Public AI Inventory page. View top apps across different categories.

AI Assets by Categories: View the newly discovered assets and risky assets. You can also view the distribution of assets across categories, like Models, MCP servers, Agents, and Apps. Click Details to be redirected to the AI Assets page.
The dashboard also displays detailed information in the following tabs:
Public AI
View the top apps across categories. Use the carousel buttons to switch between the views. Click a category to view further details on the Public AI - Inventory page.
AI Infrastructure

Use this tab to view AI-related infrastructure connected to your organization and evaluate its security posture, identify exposed or misconfigured components, and confirm that access controls, logging, and policies are configured correctly. The Asset Explorer section displays a visual summary of your AI Inventory across connected cloud accounts and repositories. Each hero node shows the count of the AI Asset Type. You can view data in the following tabs:

AI Assets: Use this tab to view an inventory of AI asset entities—models, MCP servers, agents, and apps, so you can see where AI usage is concentrated and prioritize controls. The central node shows the total AI asset count, and each hero node shows the count for a specific asset type. Select an asset type to view breakdowns by risk level, type, and environment. Click the number to open the corresponding AI Asset page for more details.

AI Resources: Use this tab to view an inventory of entities involved in AI resource usage, such as data stores, AI software libraries, AI guardrails, identities, and workloads. The central node shows the total AI resource count, and each hero node shows the count for a specific asset type. Select a resource type to view breakdowns by risk level, type, and environment. Click the number to open the corresponding AI Resources page for more details.

Data Classification for AI: Use this tab to view an inventory of entities involved in AI data classification categories, such as Source Code, Legal, and Technical. The central node shows the total items and each hero node shows the count for a data classification type. Select a data classification type to view breakdowns by subcategories. Click number to open the corresponding details on the AI Resources - Workload page.
Red Teaming
Use this tab to view the following information:
AI Asset Insights
View a breakdown of AI Assets that have been red-teamed which are categorized based on the following:
Health Score: Displays a segmented view of a health score categorized as critical, low, medium, high, or unknown.
Availability: Displays a segmented view based on whether the asset is internal or customer-facing.
Click Details to view details on the AI Red Teaming Overview page.
Untested AI Assets
View a list of AI assets that have been onboarded but have not yet been red teamed. Since no test runs have been executed, their security posture is unknown.
Recent Test Runs

View a list of AI assets on which red-teaming test runs have been executed. Click the asset name to view the details of health score, lifecycle, category score, category overview, probe run details, etc.
